evidence: createRouter builds an Express Router and registers routes such as router.post('/users', users.create) and router.put('/tasks/:taskId/assignee', tasks.assign). This is HTTP transport wiring, which belongs in infrastructure.
No conditionals, calculations or domain invariants appear in the file. Every handler is passed straight to a controller method.
The Controllers interface only groups the injected controller instances for the router.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file src/infrastructure/http/routes.ts only defines Express HTTP routes. It maps paths and verbs to controller handlers. That is transport/framework wiring, which is what the infrastructure layer is for. It has no business rules, validation, domain decisions or persistence logic. Its Controllers interface is just a dependency bag for the router.
